## Context / Problem
Rewritten after premise refutation (see comments): the observed fold-horizon race (bridge write + concurrent compact → union merge lands an event timestamped before the snapshot, absent from `source_event_uuids`) is the known RC2 class of ADR-0035, and the repair door EXISTS and works: `rebar fsck --repair-snapshots` / `fsck --repair` → `compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (full HLC-ordered log incl. `.retired`, `.snapshot-rebuild.bak` sentinel, fail-closed guard) — it healed the live incident on e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2.

The REAL defect (verified in a RED run against current main): **the next natural fold LAUNDERS the orphan.** When a ticket with an un-cited pre-snapshot event crosses the compaction threshold, the fold's whole-dir enumeration RETIRES the orphan file and CITES its uuid in the new snapshot's `source_event_uuids` — but the replay's positional skip means its effect is NOT in the compiled state. fsck then reports clean (uuid cited, file retired): repairable damage silently becomes unrepairable-by-tooling loss at the first threshold crossing after the race. The existing repair door only works in the window BEFORE that fold. Secondary gap: (G4) `fsck --repair-snapshots` rebuilds on ANY orphan type, bypassing the `_AUTO_RECOVER` vs `_HUMAN_TRIAGE` routing that `fsck --repair` enforces (fsck_repair.py:38-41, applied at :202).

## Proposed fix
1. **Stop the laundering (G1, the bug):** the natural fold (compact_txn) must EXCLUDE un-cited pre-snapshot events from both retirement and `source_event_uuids` citation — an orphan stays an unretired, un-cited file, so the fsck ORPHAN_EVENT finding and the repair window survive indefinitely. The fold does NOT absorb orphans itself (that would bypass the type routing); it defers to the repair door. Ordering note: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` replays the full log in HLC total order, so absorbed order-sensitive events are deterministic there — no new ordering semantics are introduced by this change.
2. **Routing parity (G4):** `--repair-snapshots` applies the same `_AUTO_RECOVER`/`_HUMAN_TRIAGE` routing instead of rebuilding unconditionally, so the two fsck repair paths cannot disagree about order-sensitive orphans.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py — fold enumeration excludes un-cited pre-snapshot events from retirement + citation (defer guard).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py — routing parity for --repair-snapshots (the `_AUTO_RECOVER_ORPHAN_TYPES`/`_HUMAN_TRIAGE_ORPHAN_TYPES` split already applied by `fsck --repair` at fsck_repair.py:202).
- tests/unit/test_fold_orphan_laundering.py — new: RED reproduction of the laundering (orphan retired+cited+effect-lost today), exclusion behavior, repair-window survival across a threshold-crossing fold.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A ticket with an un-cited pre-snapshot COMMENT that crosses the compaction threshold keeps the orphan unretired/un-cited and fsck still reports ORPHAN_EVENT after the fold; `fsck --repair-snapshots` afterward restores the comment to `show`; integration test.
- [ ] `--repair-snapshots` no longer rebuilds past `_HUMAN_TRIAGE` types; guard test.
- [ ] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.

## Out of scope
Writer-path auto-detection after union merge (G3 — separate follow-up if wanted); doctor-side ORPHAN_EVENT routing (doctor.py has no snapshot/orphan scan — orphan detection and repair are fsck's domain via fsck_repair.py, and adding a duplicate scan to doctor would be a parallel implementation; users are directed to `fsck --repair`); bridge/Jira duplicate policy; crash-atomicity (mantis, landed); dirty-tree repair (dormouse, landed).
